extracted.intended_audience: VA research applicants and scientific merit reviewers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for conducting and interpreting VA Merit Review evaluations of research grant applications, including scoring procedures, standard review criteria, and VA-specific eligibility/administrative considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merit Review process objective/legal basis
rubrics_metrics.description: Merit Review is an objective process of evaluating competing Federal award applications in accordance with written standards set forth by VA and in accordance with 2 C.F.R. § 200.205.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes that reviews must follow VA written standards and applicable federal regulations (2 C.F.R. § 200.205); implies impartial, documented procedures and adherence to federal merit review expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application evaluation per NOFO
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are reviewed/scored in accordance with evaluation criteria included in the Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers must use the scoring guidelines outlined in the specific NOFO; individual reviews are conducted and scored using those NOFO criteria. The NOFO supersedes generic guidance where it provides specific instructions or weights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer scoring practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers individually review and score each application using scoring guidelines outlined in the original NOFO; reviewers serving on Scientific Merit Review Board assign each application a single score reflecting their assessment of overall scientific merit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each reviewer produces an individual overall scientific merit score. Reviewers should integrate the NOFO criteria into a single overall assessment rather than submitting multiple unrelated numeric components unless the NOFO specifies otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring calculation and interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Individual reviewer scores are averaged and then multiplied by 100 to determine final score; lower score = better; threshold scores vary by service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final numeric score = mean of reviewer scores × 100. Review committees and services may adopt different funding thresholds — a lower numeric score indicates higher merit (i.e., top-ranked applications have lower scores).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scored applications (panel discussion requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications discussed at panel meeting; each receives a final overall score; score informs funding decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications selected for discussion during the panel receive full consideration and an assigned final overall score which is used to prioritize funding decisions. Being discussed is a precondition for receiving a final score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unscored applications (streamlining policy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any proposal with average preliminary score in the lower (least meritorious) 25-30% may be unscored (not discussed in panel).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications in the bottom ~25–30% based on preliminary averages are typically streamlined (not discussed) and therefore not assigned final scores; these may be appropriate for resubmission depending on written critique comments. Reviewers should still provide written critiques for these applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard criterion — Significance to Veterans
rubrics_metrics.description: Direct relevance to Veteran health or disability; mission alignment with VA priorities; potential to improve veteran care.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the extent to which the proposed research addresses an important problem for Veterans, aligns with VA priorities, and will likely lead to improvements in Veteran care or health outcomes. Consider population relevance and translational potential to VA healthcare.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard criterion — Scientific Merit
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality and innovation of the research; clear hypotheses and aims; sound experimental design; rigor and reproducibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate novelty/innovation, clarity of hypotheses and specific aims, overall scientific rationale, methodological rigor, attention to reproducibility, and whether the project advances knowledge in a meaningful way. Look for potential weaknesses in logic or design that could undermine conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard criterion — Investigator Qualifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Track record; expertise; VA appointment status (typically required - 5/8ths).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider the PI's and key personnel's prior productivity, expertise relevant to the project, and ability to execute the work. Note VA-specific expectation that investigators typically hold a paid VA appointment (commonly 5/8ths or greater) for eligibility or suitability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard criterion — Approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Methodology; feasibility; statistical analysis; power calculations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the experimental and analytical approaches are appropriate and feasible to meet the aims, including adequacy of statistical plans and sample size/power calculations. Identify risks and proposed mitigations, alternative strategies, and clarity of timelines and milestones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard criterion — Environment
rubrics_metrics.description: VA facility resources; institutional commitment; collaborations; access to veteran populations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge whether the institutional setting and available resources support successful completion (e.g., equipment, clinical/regulatory support, collaborations) and whether the proposal documents sufficient institutional commitment and access to required Veteran populations or data sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key VA consideration — PI VA appointment requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: PI must hold a paid VA appointment (typically 5/8ths or more).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility and reviewer assessment may require that the PI maintain an appropriate VA appointment fraction; lack of required appointment may render an application noncompliant or less favorable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key VA consideration — Research location and veteran access
rubrics_metrics.description: Research must be conducted at VA facility (or via approved arrangements); veteran patient population must be appropriately accessible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure proposed conduct location(s) are VA facilities or have documented, approved arrangements. Reviewers should verify that the research team has realistic and approved access to the Veteran populations necessary to complete the study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key VA consideration — Alignment with VA priorities and military-related relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Alignment with VA Office of Research and Development priorities; research relevant to military service-related conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the extent to which the application maps to OROD strategic priorities and addresses conditions or issues related to military service that are priorities for VA; stronger alignment increases relevance and potential for support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Major VA research services and funding mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Descriptions of major VA Research Services (BLR&D, CSR&D, HSR&D, RR&D) and common mechanisms (e.g., I01 Merit Review, IK1/IK2 Career Development, I21 pilot/exploratory, IIR, I50 Centers, QUERI).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should choose the mechanism appropriate to their research area and career stage; different services use similar merit review processes but may have service-specific priorities, funding thresholds, and program-specific requirements. Reviewers should consider mechanism-specific expectations when assessing proposals.
